claims.claim: Warren Buffett was born in Omaha, Nebraska, on August 30, 1930; his father Howard Buffett was a businessman and U.S. Congressman.
Charlie Munger was born in Omaha on January 1, 1924; his father Alfred Case Munger was a lawyer.
Both worked as youths in Buffett's grandfather's grocery store and did not meet until 1959.
Munger studied mathematics at the University of Michigan, left in 1943 for the U.S. Army Air Corps, and studied meteorology at Caltech through the Army.
Munger earned a J.D. magna cum laude from Harvard Law School in 1948 and moved to California, joining Wright & Garrett.

Buffett attended Wharton 1947-1949, earned a B.S. in Business Administration from the University of Nebraska, was rejected by Harvard Business School in 1950, and earned an M.S. in Economics from Columbia in 1951, choosing it because Benjamin Graham taught there.
Buffett worked at Graham-Newman Corp. as a securities analyst from 1954 to 1956 and created Buffett Partnership Ltd. in 1956; it was liquidated in 1969 with Berkshire shares passed to partners.
Munger co-founded Munger, Tolles & Olson and Wheeler, Munger and Company in 1962 and gave up law to manage investments.
Wheeler, Munger and Co. lost 32% in 1973 and 31% in 1974 and was wound up in 1976.
Buffett and Munger met in 1959, introduced by an Omaha doctor.
Buffett first bought Berkshire shares in 1962.
After the tender price dispute with Seabury Stanton, Buffett bought more shares and formally took control at an early-May 1965 board meeting; Berkshire was a New England textile manufacturer.
Buffett became chairman and CEO of Berkshire in 1970.
Munger pushed Buffett from buying fair businesses at wonderful prices to wonderful businesses at fair prices, away from Graham's approach.

See's Candies was bought in 1972 for $25 million through Blue Chip Stamps, in which Munger, Buffett and Berkshire had stakes; the sellers asked $30 million and Buffett wrote that his caution could have scuttled the purchase.
Munger became vice chairman of Berkshire Hathaway in 1978.
Munger was chairman of Wesco Financial from 1984 to 2011; Poor Charlie's Almanack was published in 2005.
The annual meeting is held in Omaha, with leadership answering shareholder questions.
Buffett called not tendering his Berkshire shares in 1964 a monumentally stupid decision and closed the textile operation in 1985.
Dexter Shoe was bought in 1993 for $433 million in Berkshire stock and Buffett called it the worst deal he had made.
Munger died at a California hospital on November 28, 2023.
Munger died 33 days before his 100th birthday; Buffett called him the architect of Berkshire and himself the general contractor.
On May 3, 2025, at the annual meeting in Omaha, Buffett announced he would step down as CEO at the end of the year; Greg Abel to become CEO on January 1, 2026.
In September 2026 Buffett stepped down as chairman, was succeeded by his son Howard Buffett, became chairman emeritus and remained a director.
Buffett received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2011.

quotes.text: It took Charlie Munger to break my cigar-butt habits and set the course for building a business that could combine huge size with satisfactory profits.
quotes.source: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter for 2014 (published 2015)

quotes.text: Forget what you know about buying fair businesses at wonderful prices; instead, buy wonderful businesses at fair prices.
quotes.source: Warren Buffett, stating the blueprint Munger gave him, Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter for 2014 (published 2015)

quotes.text: To date, Dexter is the worst deal that I've made.
quotes.source: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter for 2007 (published 2008)

uncertain: Exact date Buffett stepped down as chairman: Wikipedia and the URLs of NPR, Washington Post, Bloomberg, Axios and CNBC reports give September 18, 2026; the one news page fetched in full (Carrier Management, a Bloomberg reprint) is dated September 21. The profile says only 'September 2026'. Berkshire's own 2026 news page and most major news sites blocked fetching, so this rests on one fetched reprint plus Wikipedia.
The 'wonderful businesses at fair prices' line is Buffett's wording of Munger's advice, not a verified verbatim Munger quote. The 2023 letter gives a different wording and dates the advice to 1965.
Munger's place of death: Wikipedia says Santa Barbara, California; Berkshire's release says only 'a California hospital'. The profile uses the release wording.
Annual meeting attendance figures differ between sources (over 20,000 versus over 40,000) and were left out.
The name of Buffett's grandfather and of the grocery store (Buffett & Son) appears on Wikipedia's Munger page only; the profile says 'the grocery store owned by Buffett's grandfather'.
The year Buffett received his University of Nebraska degree is shown inconsistently and was left out. The year Munger stopped practicing law was not found and was left out.
Berkshire letters at berkshirehathaway.com were downloaded as PDFs and read with pdftotext, since WebFetch could not parse them; quotes were checked against that extracted text.
Britannica, AP, CNBC, CBC and Washington Post pages could not be fetched (403 or blocked), so biographical details for early life rely on Wikipedia plus Buffett's letters.
